subject: ACME: request-drain / tail-latency impact — exec briefing and mitigation
content:
From: Jamal Baker <jamal.baker@acme-corp.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-16 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Checkout latency spikes + errors (p99) — urgent

Hi Avery / Marissa,

Over the last 2 hours our checkout path p99 latency has jumped from ~420ms to 2.1s, and we're seeing a 1.3% spike in 5xx errors. This correlates with a large promotional traffic burst but the behavior looks like requests are piling up behind the Redwood inference layer — tail latency, not model decode time. Our cart abandonment rate already increased. Can your team confirm whether something on your side (queueing/concurrency caps/backpressure) is throttling or stalling requests?

I've attached a small trace slice and logs. Ops oncall is standing by: ops+oncall@acme-corp.com.

Thanks,
Jamal
Jamal Baker
SRE Lead, Acme Commerce

-----
From: avery_johnson@redwood.com
To: Jamal Baker <jamal.baker@acme-corp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-16 10:05 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spikes + errors (p99) — urgent

Jamal — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're pulling immediate traces from the request router and the P2 pool that handles the model variant you call. Initial ask: can you share the exact sample request IDs that map to the 5xx errors? We'll triage overlap with our KV cache hits and batching queue.

Immediate actions from our side:
- Rishi is looking at queue depth and recent routing changes.
- I'll authorize a temporary increase to the concurrency cap for your account if we confirm it's safe.
- If needed we can switch your route to a dedicated burst pool for the next 2 hours while the promo continues.

I'll keep you posted every 30 minutes.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, Jamal Baker <jamal.baker@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2028-03-16 13:30 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spikes + errors (p99) — initial analysis

Quick summary of what we see from the serving side (short):
- Queue depth on the p2-general GPU pool for ACME route jumped ~6x starting at 08:45 PST.
- Batching windows expanded (requests waited longer for a batch to fill), which increased non-decode wait time.
- Several long-running KV cache misses triggered cold-loads that blocked read lanes; this created backpressure and a small number of requests hit the concurrency cap and were rejected (5xx).

Evidence attached: p99_tail_dashboard.png and a filtered tail log slice.

Immediate mitigation options (we recommend doing steps 1 & 3 now):
1) Increase account concurrency cap from 60 -> 120 for the next 3 hours (safe given spare capacity in us-west pool).
2) Roll back a recent router tweak that changed prefix routing (low confidence as cause).
3) Enable prefix/KV caching aggressive mode for ACME route (reduces cold-loads).
4) Route heavy batchers to a segregated pool or apply client-side leaky-bucket (longer-term).

I'm attaching the logs we pulled and a short runbook snippet.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: avery_johnson@redwood.com

Cc: Jamal Baker <jamal.baker@acme-corp.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-17 11:02 AM -0700
Subject: Exec briefing: ACME checkout long-tail impact + recommended actions

Team — summarizing for exec attention and decision:

What happened:
- Promotional traffic caused an atypical request distribution (many small requests + a few large batch inference requests).
- Our router's batching heuristic plus several cold KV cache misses created queueing on the p2 pool and a short-lived request drain/backpressure event.
- When per-account concurrency cap was reached some requests returned 5xx rather than being queued gracefully.

Customer impact:
- Reported 1.3% increase in 5xx and p99 rising to ~2.1s for checkout flows during the peak window.
- Visible conversion hit for the promo window (Acme reports measurable revenue impact).

Recommended immediate actions (for approval):
1) Approve temporary concurrency cap increase (60->120) for the next 6 hours and monitor.
2) Route ACME to a reserved burst pool for promo hours (cost-bearing by Redwood for goodwill; ACME committed to discuss in MMP).
3) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for ACME route and invalidate warmers after change.
4) Short term: apply leaky-bucket at the router to smooth large batchers.
5) Postmortem + action items to ensure graceful degradation (fail-open to quantized variant) and update runbooks.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx — contains timeline and owner assignments. I also attached the logs from Rishi.

Asking for a quick go/no-go so we can implement steps 1 & 3 within the hour.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
